entities.summary:
Yonsei University, established in 1957 in Seoul, South Korea, stands as one of the foremost private institutions of higher education in East Asia. It is part of the prestigious 'SKY' universities, which includes Seoul National University and Korea University, collectively representing the elite academic landscape of South Korea. The founders, including the prominent Christian missionary Horace Grant Underwood, aimed to create an institution that not only provided rigorous academic training but also contributed to the moral and social development of Korean society, especially in the aftermath of the Korean War (1950-1953). Today, Yonsei remains a pivotal force in shaping the educational and cultural fabric of modern South Korea, with campuses in both Seoul and Incheon.

Throughout its history, Yonsei University has achieved numerous milestones, contributing significantly to various fields such as science, technology, and the humanities. The university has produced over 300,000 graduates, including influential leaders in politics, business, and academia, such as former South Korean President Kim Dae-jung and notable business leaders like Lee Jay-hyun of CJ Group. The institution has expanded its international outreach through various exchange programs and partnerships, fostering a global perspective among its students and faculty. Notably, Yonsei hosted the first International Conference on Asian Studies in 2007, emphasizing its commitment to advancing academic discourse on a global scale.
